newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Late exporter dollar sales and players liquidating long dollar positions ahead of the long weekend helped the South African rand over one-and-a-half cents firmer on Wednesday after another quiet, pre-festive season day.
It ended at 4.6680/6730 on the dollar from 4.6840/6890 late on Tuesday but forex traders said it was likely the unit would drift weaker again at the Thursday start on importer dollar demand.

The rand started the day stronger, buoyed by New York dollar inflows and hovered around the 4.6760 level for most of the morning before dipping below 4.67 in the late afternoon as dollars flowed into the market.
"A lot of guys rid themselves of long dollar positions in anticipation of the long weekend and we also saw exporters selling dollars," a trader at one of the "big four" banks said.
However, he believed the gains would be short-lived and the the rand would drift weaker to above 4.67 again at the Thursday start on importer dollar demand.
Another trader cautioned that there was still some potential for volatility until next Friday when the festive season started in earnest.

"Overall it looks as if we've had it for the year but there could still be a bit of volatility up until the end of next week," he said, adding however that the rand should hold below 4.70 in a 4.65 to 4.70 range until year-end.
News that telecomunications utility Telkom would announce a foreign equity partner by March next year also helped the rand, traders said.
The sale of a stake in Telkom to foreign bidders is the first major step in the South African government's privatisation programme and is seen as a litmus test of its commitment to economic reform.
Against the crosses, the rand was last quoted at 7.7367/7497 against sterling from 7.7235/7364 previously and at 0.3300/3304 marks from 0.3310/3314 marks.
Key long bonds ended slightly weaker as the market tracked U.S. Treasuries in the absence of fresh news at home.
At 1429 GMT government's R150 stock was at 15.96 percent from 15.93 percent overnight after holding around previous closing levels for most of the day.
Bond traders said yields ticked slightly higher in the afternoon after U.S. Treasuries tumbled on the back of investors selling Treasuries in favour of corporates as well as foreign selling.
The yield on the 30-year T-bond was last at 6.56 percent.
Local bond traders expected the South African market to open flattish to slightly stronger on Thursday and to hold in a 15.85 to 15.96 percent range on the day.
Bond Exchange statistics showed foreigners were net sellers of 13.46 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Tuesday after buying 97.12 million rand on Monday.
Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at 1.48 billion rand on Tuesday -- a reflection of the winding down of activity ahead of the holiday period -- from 4.99 billion rand on Monday.

On the money market, three-month NCD rates were quoted steady at between 17.20 to 17.25 percent offered, while the 90-day BA rate moved higher to between 16.55 and 16.90 percent from 16.55 and 16.80 percent.
The Reserve Bank indicated the money market shortage slightly lower at 9.132 billion rand on Tuesday from 9.340 billion rand on Monday.
-- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
